description:
FILED s535a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from a span-port probe (scratch/s535a/pr/p15.pl in the s535a worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: main 06a4b8ba and the s535a tree print the same wrong answer -- the span pass never sees it.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    use feature "state"; state $st = 1;
    package Foo;
    print "st=$st\n";

perl:              st=1
main / s535a:      st=        -- SILENT WRONG

WHY (read): a FILE-level `state` is outside _rename_state_vars' classic subset, so the state source prepass (_rewrite_state_prepass -> _state_rewrite_routes) rewrites it BEFORE the binder is built: the decl becomes a guarded init of fresh cells `$st__state__0` / `..__init`, and every later use is renamed to the cell.  Those cells are left UNDECLARED on purpose ("become defvar'd package globals via _forward_global_decls"), i.e. a global of the SECTION package: the main section defcells `$st__state__0`, the Foo section's read is `Foo::$st__state__0` -- another variable.  The span pass cannot help: by the time it runs the name is a package global, not a lexical.

FIX DIRECTION (not designed): the prepass's file-CV cells are the declaring section's: spell the post-section uses package-qualified (`$main::st__state__0`), the way the span renamer qualifies a promoted lexical's later-section uses -- or declare the cells and let the span pass see the state binding (the binder records kind `state`).  Name-resolution change: the sweep is the gate.

=== DONE (s536e) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, generation v2-12900; commit 23baa13b).  The state prepass's unwrapped cells (`$st__state__0`, file CV / named sub) are globals of the DECLARING package; a use the prepass's own binder places in another package (a later `package NAME;` section, a `package NAME { }` block, an in-block `package` statement) is now spelled `$Decl::st__state__0` -- `Pl/Parser2.pm` `_state_qualify_foreign_uses`, called from `_state_rewrite_routes` for every non-anon route (Symbols + interpolated text; `${x}` braces are refused by `_state_rw_blocker` already).  Probed perl -> base -> tree (scratch/s536e/pr/m2*.pl): the reproducer + a sub incrementing it twice, a loop body with an in-block `package`, a `package Bar { sub inc }` block, an in-block + a section package writing it; controls: a named sub's state across an in-sub `package`, anon-sub state -- tree = perl.  The eval('$st') residue (a state cell is not reachable from eval by its original name, same section too) is pre-existing and documented in the prepass header.  Guard span-binder-01.t rows 27-29 (fail on the base).  Emission: t/op/lexsub.t (`state $stuff` read from a `package A { state sub foo { $stuff .= ... } }` block -- its two companion rows 67 / 130 checked by a one-file run).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a FILE-level `state $x` read in a later top-level `package` section reads an EMPTY variable -- the state prepass's fresh cells are globals of the SECTION package (pre-existing, not the span pass)
